text:
Nashville has won four straight, and the chances back it: 55% of the expected goals in those games, with Juuse Saros at .912 and 6.3 goals saved above expected after a rough 2025-26. Roman Josi is one point from 800 for his career, and the Predators just reshaped their young core, sending Matthew Wood to Seattle for Shane Wright, who fit in right away beside Filip Forsberg according to the headlines. Steven Stamkos, now in the all-time top five for power-play goals, is 37% to score.

Los Angeles is the opposite story: a team playing better than its 12 points. Our playoff model has the Kings at 16.6 expected points, more than four above what they have, and they took 58% of the expected goals during a 2-3-0 week. The problem has been in net. Darcy Kuemper, who would play his 500th NHL game, is at .878 and five goals worse than expected. Mats Zuccarello is out, so Artemi Panarin has taken his spot beside Erik Haula and Alex Laferriere, and Corey Perry is up to 16 and a half minutes a night. Haula faces Nashville for the first time since leaving.

Our numbers call it close, 3.08 to 2.98 for Los Angeles. Nashville gets a lot of its offense from Josi, Forsberg and Ryan O'Reilly, all 27% or better for two points. For the Kings, Adrian Kempe (38% to score) is coming off a hat trick against San Jose, and Panarin is 74% for a point. Our sleeper is Quinton Byfield, 50% for a point, above his season pace. Jonathan Marchessault is day-to-day and could return for Nashville.
headline: Predators keep rolling; Kings keep waiting

hunch.text: One team's record is ahead of its play, the other's is behind. Our hunch is the Kings' process finally shows up on the scoreboard, and Nashville's streak stops at four.
